NEOX|A (ip): RISC-V-based AI/ML accelerator IP for low-power edge inference.
NEOX|G (ip): RISC-V-based programmable GPU IP combining graphics and compute for edge devices.
NEMA|dc display controllers (ip): Low-power display controller IP for small screens in wearables and IoT.
NemaGFX SDK (sdk): Graphics/compute software stack and drivers for Think Silicon GPU IP.
differentiator: Among the smallest, lowest-power GPU IP cores; RISC-V NEOX line merges graphics with AI acceleration.

name: Beijing Tsingmicro Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. (Tsing Micro)
focus: Coarse-grained reconfigurable AI processors from edge voice/vision chips to datacenter accelerators
problem: Fixed-function AI chips waste energy and cannot adapt efficiently to fast-changing AI models at the edge.
products: TX2 series (chip): Ultra-low-power reconfigurable edge AI chips for voice and sensing in consumer/IoT devices.
TX5 series (chip): Edge vision AI chips for face recognition, cameras and smart terminals.
TX8 series (chip): High-performance reconfigurable AI chips for datacenter LLM training and inference.
TX8-based accelerator cards and servers (system): Compute cards/servers built on TX8 chips for domestic AI computing clusters.
differentiator: China's leading reconfigurable-computing (CGRA) AI chip company, Tsinghua spinout, spanning edge to datacenter.

name: Ubitium GmbH
focus: Workload-agnostic universal RISC-V processor unifying CPU, GPU, DSP, FPGA and AI functions
problem: Embedded products need several costly chips (CPU, GPU, DSP, NPU) to add AI, raising BOM and complexity.
products: Universal RISC-V Processor (chip): Single reconfigurable array chip handling CPU, GPU, DSP, FPGA and AI workloads; first silicon targeted 2026.
Prototype chips and development kits (system): Early dev kits for evaluating the universal processor in embedded designs.
differentiator: One homogeneous processor array replaces multiple specialized units, promising AI at no added silicon cost.

name: UNISOC (Shanghai) Technologies Co., Ltd.
focus: Affordable 4G/5G smartphone, wearable, IoT and automotive SoCs with on-chip AI
problem: Budget phones and IoT devices need on-device AI without the cost of premium flagship chipsets.
products: T-series smartphone SoCs (incl. Tanggula 5G T760/T770) (chip): 4G/5G mobile SoCs with integrated NPU for on-device camera, voice and AI features.
W-series wearable SoCs (e.g., W517) (chip): Smartwatch/wearable platforms with low-power processing for on-device features.
A-series automotive SoCs (e.g., A7870) (chip): Smart-cockpit SoCs for in-vehicle infotainment and AI functions.
Cellular IoT chips (chip): Cat.1/NB-IoT/5G RedCap modem SoCs for connected IoT devices.
differentiator: China's largest merchant mobile SoC vendor, dominant in low-cost phones and cellular IoT globally.

name: Untether AI Corporation
focus: At-memory compute inference chips and cards for energy-efficient edge and datacenter AI
problem: Moving data between memory and compute dominates AI inference energy, limiting performance per watt.
products: speedAI240 (Boqueria) (chip): Second-gen at-memory inference chip, ~2 PetaFLOPs FP8; discontinued 2025.
runAI200 (chip): First-gen at-memory compute inference chip (2020).
tsunAImi accelerator cards (system): PCIe inference cards for edge/on-prem servers built on Untether chips.
imAIgine SDK (sdk): Compiler and runtime toolchain for deploying models on Untether accelerators.
differentiator: At-memory architecture placing RISC-V processing elements beside SRAM for very high inference TOPS/W.

name: VeriSilicon Microelectronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.
focus: Processor IP (NPU, GPU, ISP, VPU, DSP) and turnkey custom silicon for edge AI chips
problem: Chipmakers need proven AI and multimedia IP and design services to build edge AI SoCs quickly.
products: Vivante NPU IP (VIP9000 family) (ip): Scalable neural processing unit IP for on-device inference in SoCs.
Nano NPU IP (VIP9000Nano) (ip): Ultra-low-power NPU IP for wearables and always-on IoT devices.
Vivante GPU / GPGPU IP (ip): Graphics and compute GPU IP, including AI-oriented GPGPU cores.
ISP and Hantro VPU IP (ip): Image signal processing and video codec IP for cameras and vision pipelines.
ZSP DSP IP (ip): Digital signal processor IP for audio, voice and sensor processing.
Custom silicon / chiplet design services (service): Turnkey ASIC and chiplet design-to-production services for AI SoCs.
differentiator: Broad one-stop processor IP portfolio plus design services; NPU IP licensed into a large base of edge SoCs.

name: Witmem Technology (WITINMEM, Beijing Zhicun Technology / 知存科技)
focus: Analog compute-in-memory (flash) AI chips for wearables, hearables and IoT
problem: Always-on AI in earbuds and wearables drains batteries when data shuttles between memory and processor.
products: WTM2101 (chip): Compute-in-flash AI SoC for sub-mW voice recognition, denoising and health sensing.
WTM8 series (chip): Higher-performance compute-in-memory chips targeting vision and AR/edge workloads.
WTM2101 development kit and toolchain (sdk): Tools to map neural networks onto Witmem compute-in-memory arrays.
differentiator: Among the first to mass-produce analog compute-in-flash AI chips for consumer devices.

name: XMOS Ltd
focus: Software-defined multicore xcore processors for voice, audio and edge AI
problem: Device makers need cheap, deterministic processors that add local voice and AI without extra chips or cloud.
products: xcore.ai (chip): Third-gen crossover multicore processor with vector unit for edge AI, from ~$1.
XVF3800 / XVF3610 voice processors (chip): Far-field voice processors with beamforming, AEC and local keyword spotting.
XMOS AI tools (sdk): Toolchain to optimize and deploy TensorFlow Lite models on xcore.
XCORE GenSoC platform (platform): 2025 repositioning letting developers describe system behaviour in natural language on xcore.
differentiator: Deterministic real-time multicore architecture combining I/O, DSP, control and AI in one low-cost chip.

name: ByteDance Ltd. (AIBrix)
focus: Open-source Kubernetes-native infrastructure for scalable, cost-efficient self-hosted LLM serving
problem: Running vLLM at production scale on own Kubernetes clusters needs routing, autoscaling and KV-cache management.
products: AIBrix (platform): Open-source control plane for vLLM: LLM gateway, LoRA management, autoscaling, distributed KV cache.
differentiator: Battle-tested inside ByteDance's production LLM serving and co-designed with the vLLM community.

name: Anyscale, Inc.
focus: Ray-based distributed compute platform for scaling AI training, data processing and inference
problem: Scaling AI workloads across many GPUs and nodes requires complex distributed-systems engineering.
products: Ray (open source) (runtime): Distributed compute framework for AI; transferred to PyTorch Foundation in late 2025.
Ray Serve / Ray Serve LLM (runtime): Scalable model and LLM serving library, integrates vLLM; deployable on own clusters.
Anyscale Platform (BYOC) (platform): Managed Ray platform deployable into customer AWS, GCP or Azure accounts.
RayTurbo (runtime): Anyscale's optimized proprietary Ray runtime for faster, cheaper workloads.
KubeRay (platform): Kubernetes operator for running Ray clusters on own infrastructure.
differentiator: Created Ray, among the most widely used open-source engines for distributed AI workloads.

name: Approaching.AI (趋境科技)
focus: Heterogeneous CPU-GPU inference that makes frontier-size open LLMs affordable on local hardware

products: KTransformers (runtime): Open-source framework offloading MoE experts to CPU/DRAM to run DeepSeek-class models on one GPU.
ATaaS token production platform (service): AI-token-as-a-service inference capacity platform built on its heterogeneous inference stack.
LLM inference appliances (all-in-one machines) (system): On-prem inference servers bundling KTransformers optimizations for enterprise deployment (reported).
differentiator: Tsinghua-linked expert-offloading technique lets trillion-parameter-class MoE models run on one workstation.

name: Arc Compute
focus: GPU utilization and performance-management software for AI/HPC infrastructure
problem: Expensive on-prem GPUs sit underutilized, wasting capital and limiting AI throughput.
products: ArcHPC (platform): GPU task-matching and utilization software that raises throughput on bare-metal AI/HPC servers.
GPU server solutions (system): NVIDIA HGX-class GPU servers supplied with ArcHPC (reported, details unverified).
differentiator: Low-level GPU workload matching to squeeze more throughput from existing hardware.

name: Avesha, Inc.
focus: Kubernetes multi-cluster and GPU orchestration for hybrid AI infrastructure
problem: GPU capacity is stranded in silos across clusters, leaving AI teams short while GPUs sit idle.
products: Elastic GPU Service (EGS) (platform): Dynamic GPU orchestration, reallocation and bursting across on-prem and cloud clusters.
KubeSlice (platform): Open-source multi-cluster Kubernetes networking and tenancy layer.
Smart Scaler (platform): AI-driven predictive autoscaling for Kubernetes workloads.
SUSE AI + EGS blueprint (platform): Joint reference architecture combining EGS with SUSE AI for private AI.
differentiator: Treats GPUs across multiple clusters and clouds as one elastic, shareable pool.

name: Baseten, Inc.
focus: High-performance production inference for open, custom and fine-tuned models

Baseten Self-hosted (platform): Runs Baseten's inference stack inside the customer's own VPC/cloud account.
Baseten Hybrid (platform): Combines customer-owned compute with burst to Baseten Cloud.
Truss (sdk): Open-source model packaging framework for deploying models anywhere.
Chains (sdk): Framework for multi-model, multi-step inference workflows.

name: Beam Cloud, Inc. (Beam)

products: Beam Cloud (platform): Managed serverless GPU platform for inference endpoints, jobs and sandboxes.
beta9 (runtime): Open-source (AGPL) serverless GPU engine self-hostable on own GPUs/Kubernetes across clouds.
differentiator: Open-source Modal alternative whose engine can run serverless GPU workloads on any infrastructure.

name: BentoML (Atalaya Tech, Inc.)

products: Friendli Inference Engine (runtime): Optimized LLM/multimodal serving engine with iteration-level batching and custom kernels.

Friendli Dedicated Endpoints (platform): Managed dedicated GPU deployments of custom and open models.

GPUStack enterprise services (service): Commercial deployment, domestic-chip adaptation and support for 250+ enterprise customers.
differentiator: Broad heterogeneous hardware support incl. Chinese NPUs; 110k+ users in 121 countries.

problem: Enterprises running open LLMs at scale face high cost per token and data-control concerns.
products: Impala inference platform (platform): Proprietary engine giving a serverless experience for LLMs within the customer's own VPC.
differentiator: Claims up to 13x lower cost per token while data stays in the customer's cloud account.
